GS.thesis_one_line: Premier global investment bank riding a record trading and dealmaking cycle, cheap on headline multiples but priced for that cycle to mostly persist.
kill_criteria: Standardized CET1 ratio below 11.5% for two consecutive quarters.
GBM (Global Banking & Markets) net revenues down >15% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
Annualised ROE below 12% for two consecutive quarters.
An adverse 1MDB/Malaysia arbitration ruling requiring a cash payment >$500M.
Quarterly common dividend cut or suspended (current $5.00/share).
key_adverse_facts: Standardized CET1 fell to 12.5% in 1Q26 from 14.3% (4Q25) and recovered to 12.9% in 2Q26; the supplementary leverage ratio fell two quarters (5.2% to 4.6% to 4.3%). [Corrected 2026-10-08 DV19: earlier text said CET1 fell two consecutive quarters.]
GBM (trading + banking) is ~76% of net revenues; the franchise's ROE gains are concentrated in cyclical, not fee-based, businesses.
Live 1MDB/Malaysia arbitration: Government of Malaysia demanded a further ~$1bn payment (Aug 2025) under GS's 2020 settlement guarantee; unresolved.
4Q25 net revenues fell 3.0% YoY on a $2.26bn Apple Card portfolio markdown tied to exiting that partnership (largely offset by a reserve release, but a real one-off).
data_conflicts: Triage (Q05) cited trailing ROE of 16.9%; verified current run-rate ROE is materially higher and rising (14.2% to 23.5% over the last four quarters), so the triage's 'cheap for the quality' framing understated recent quality even as it raises the question of durability.
GS.confidence_in_thesis: medium (financial trend is unambiguous and well-documented; durability of ~20%+ ROE through a capital-markets downturn is the open question, and the reverse-valuation math is sensitive to the cost-of-equity assumption) [DV19 2026-10-08: verdict changed from INCLUDE-SMALL to WATCH on valuation grounds.]

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: GS has no V1 systematic valuation row (not in the 92-name V1 universe). I reverse-engineered a P/B-ROE justified-multiple view instead: current 2.5x P/B requires ~22% sustained ROE, versus consensus-implied (~20%) and my own base case (~19%) durable ROE once the capital-markets cycle normalizes some; the gap is modest and sensitive to the cost-of-equity input, so I call the stock fair/in-line rather than cheap or expensive. [Corrected 2026-10-08 DV19: re-test with price/book 2.544x on BVPS $367.67, cost of equity 10.5% and g 3% needs ~22.1% sustained ROE vs base 19-20% (justified value $784-$833, price 12-19% above); H1 ROE ex share-based-award tax benefit is ~20.0%; base 3-year return +5% a year is below the cost of equity. implied_vs_base above; verdict INCLUDE-SMALL changed to WATCH, as DV13 did for DLR.]

PGR.thesis_one_line: The largest and most data-driven US auto insurer, still growing policies 7% a year with combined ratios 7-10 points inside its own profitability ceiling.
kill_criteria: Quarterly GAAP combined ratio above 96 (the company's own ceiling) for two consecutive quarters.
Net premiums earned growth turns negative YoY for two consecutive quarters.
Companywide policies-in-force growth turns negative YoY.
A second state imposes a profit-cap policyholder-credit resulting in a single-quarter charge >$500M.
Debt-to-total-capital ratio exceeds the company's own 30% policy ceiling.
Early-warning (added 5 Oct 2026, RA3): any single month's combined ratio above 95, or a trailing-three-month combined ratio above 92.
key_adverse_facts: A Florida statutory profit cap on personal-auto insurance forced a $950M one-time 'policyholder credit' accrual in September 2025, payable to ~2.7M Florida policyholders in early 2026; this mechanism resets each three-year window and can recur.
Premium growth has decelerated every quarter for a year (net premiums earned +14% YoY 3Q25 to +6% YoY 2Q26) as 2023-24 rate increases lap.
Open multi-state class actions (classes already certified in three states) allege improper total-loss vehicle valuation practices.

Margin has turned: July 2026 combined ratio 86.8 (+1.5 pts YoY, net income -12%) and August 89.3 (+6.2 pts, net income -22%); YTD net income $8,041m vs $8,052m on 7% more premium earned; YTD comprehensive income $6,503m vs $9,696m on -$1.54bn of fixed-income unrealised losses (monthly 8-Ks of 19 Aug and 18 Sep 2026; the dossier's sources stop at the June release).

The 87.2 YTD combined ratio includes $1.39bn of favourable prior-year reserve development (about 2.4 points), so the underlying ratio is ~89.6; the price needs a sustained ROE of ~19.9% at an 8% cost of equity (combined ratio about 93-94).
The 10-Q for Q2 2026 states $1.2bn of Florida policyholder credits were paid in Q1 2026, above the $950M accrued in Sep 2025 that the dossier cites.
data_conflicts: The d4 live-snapshot's pe_ntm (0.27) and eps_ntm ($747.86, implying >5,000% forward EPS growth) fields for PGR are confirmed data-pipeline errors, consistent with and extending the Q06 triage's own flag; neither was used in this valuation, which relies on trailing P/E and a from-filings combined-ratio/ROE build instead.
PGR.confidence_in_thesis: medium - monthly SEC disclosure gives a clean read, and that read now shows margin and net income turning down from a peak; the price still needs only ~19.9% ROE (combined ratio ~93-94) against an underlying ~89.6, but the cushion is thinner than the dossier showed

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: PGR has no V1 systematic valuation row (not in the 92-name V1 universe). Reverse-engineered via justified P/B (P/B=(ROE-g)/(COE-g)): the current 3.5x P/B requires only ~18.7% sustained ROE against a delivered TTM ROE of ~36% and a combined ratio that has stayed 86-90 for four straight quarters; the market appears to be pricing a much larger fade in profitability than the disclosed trend supports. RESTATED 5 Oct 2026 (RA3): at 31 Aug 2026 book value per share of $60.92 (August release) the price-to-book is 3.37x; with the 10-year Treasury at 5.17% (FRED, 25 Sep 2026) and an 8.0% cost of equity (7.5% and 8.5% shown), g=3%, the sustained ROE required is ~19.9% (18.2% / 21.6%), equal to a combined ratio of about 93-94 depending on equity of $35-38bn (own arithmetic reconciled to YTD pretax income of $10,211m). Underlying combined ratio ~89.6 (87.2 less 2.4 pts of reserve releases) implies ROE ~26-28%, so implied_vs_base stays below but with a cushion of roughly 5-8 ROE points, not 17.

PGR.scenario_basis: 3-year (to Sep 2029) annualised from the 25 Sep 2026 price of $205.50: net premiums earned $86bn run-rate growing 3%/5%/7% a year, combined ratio 95/90/87.5 (bear/base/bull; YTD Aug 2026 87.2 includes 2.4 pts of reserve releases so 90 is the underlying level), investment income net of interest $3.5bn growing 5% a year, tax 21.25%, diluted shares -1% a year; year-3 EPS $12.3/$19.6/$24.1 vs TTM $19.30; exit P/E 10x/12x/13x (about 10.7x trailing now); plus 0.2% regular dividend. Own arithmetic; the base is conservative against a justified P/B implied by ROE of about 25%.

ALGN.thesis_one_line: The dominant clear-aligner maker at its cheapest valuation in 14 years, but that trough partly reflects real, disclosed growth deceleration, not just neglect.
kill_criteria: Quarterly Clear Aligner volume growth turns negative YoY.
FY2026 GAAP operating-margin guidance is cut again below the current 15.1%-15.6% range (excluding charges already disclosed as of this dossier).
Full-year revenue growth guidance is cut below the current 3%-4% range.
Net cash (cash minus debt) falls below $500M.
Cumulative UK VAT / Section 122 tariff cash outflows exceed $150M beyond the $37.5M already reserved.
key_adverse_facts: FY2026 GAAP operating-margin guidance was cut from 'slightly below 18.0%' to '15.1%-15.6%' between the Q1'26 and Q2'26 releases (a ~250-290bps cut), driven by a $37.5M UK VAT contingent liability, ~$30.6M of legal settlements, and restructuring/accelerated depreciation; non-GAAP margin guidance (~23.7%) was left unchanged.

UK Upper Tribunal (2026-07-07) overturned a prior ruling that clear aligners were VAT-exempt; ALGN is now charging UK VAT from Sept 2026 and intends to appeal, with the outcome explicitly described by the company as uncertain.

ALGN is subject to Section 122 (Trade Act of 1974) tariffs following a Supreme Court ruling that its prior IEEPA tariffs were unlawful; the replacement tariffs are themselves under separate, unresolved litigation.
Two restructuring programs within twelve months (initiated 4Q24 and again 3Q25).
data_conflicts: V1 (systematic) rates ALGN 'attractive' with a base-case 3-year annualised return of +59.65%, built on 15.6%/yr revenue growth (4x the company's own 3-4% FY26 guide) and an exit multiple re-rating from 12.0x to 39.4x; V1's own street-target sanity check shows this base case ($597 in 3 years) exceeds even the Street's current 12-month high target ($240). I attribute the anomaly to V1's reverse-DCF using a TTM EBIT margin (13.2%) depressed by 3Q25/4Q25 one-offs, and use a materially more conservative base case instead (4-6% growth, partial multiple re-rating to 15-17x).
ALGN.confidence_in_thesis: medium (balance sheet and buyback support are unambiguous; the multiple-cheapness and reverse-DCF signals genuinely disagree and the resolution depends on management delivering the FY27 margin-recovery commitment)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: I agree ALGN's 12.0x NTM P/E is genuinely at the 1st percentile of its own 14-year history, but I reject V1's base-case return and 39.4x exit multiple as not credible given the company's own 3-4% guided growth and the street-target sanity check V1 itself flags; my own base case (4-6% growth, partial re-rating to 15-17x) is materially more conservative and treats the valuation as fair/in-line rather than cheap.
